14233.title: Released binaries have High severity CVEs due to Go version 1.24.1
14233.feasibility_reason: The issue points directly to upgrading the Go toolchain version in the Dockerfile and go.mod to resolve high severity CVEs in standard library dependencies.
14233.problem_summary: Prebuilt binaries contain high-severity standard library vulnerabilities (e.g., in crypto/tls, os, net/url, and archive/zip) because they were compiled using an outdated Go toolchain version.
14233.root_cause_hypothesis: The Go version pinned in go.mod, Dockerfile, and CI/release workflows specifies a Go release with known standard library vulnerabilities.
14233.suggested_approach: Upgrade the Go toolchain directive in go.mod, Dockerfile, and GitHub Actions workflow files to a patched Go release that resolves the reported CVEs.
prerequisites: Installed Go toolchain matching the target updated version
implementation_steps: Update the `go` and/or `toolchain` directives in `go.mod` to the target patched Go version.
Update any Go version references or base image tags in `Dockerfile`.
Update the Go version specified in GitHub Actions CI and release workflow files under `.github/workflows/` (e.g., `actions/setup-go` step configurations).
Run `go mod tidy` and build the binary locally using the updated Go toolchain.
Run `govulncheck -mode=binary bin/ollama` (or on the compiled target) to verify that all standard library vulnerabilities have been resolved.
Execute test suites (`go test ./...`) to ensure compatibility and lack of regressions with the updated Go version.

15669.title: Both `qwen3.5:35b-a3b-coding-bf16` and `qwen3.6:35b-a3b-coding-bf16` are labeled as non-MLX, yet they are meant for macOS only
15669.feasibility_reason: The issue is a metadata bug where specific model tags are incorrectly configured or labeled regarding their OS restrictions on the server/registry side, or the client handling of MLX/macOS requirements. Fixing model manifest requirements or catalog labels is straightforward.
15669.problem_summary: Users on Linux cannot pull certain GGUF/non-MLX model variants (e.g., qwen3.5/3.6, gemma4), failing with '412: this model requires macOS'.
15669.root_cause_hypothesis: The Ollama registry checks client platform requirements against the model manifest metadata. The affected model tags were either incorrectly published with macOS/darwin OS constraints in their manifest, or the registry's compatibility validation / MLX detection heuristics erroneously classified standard GGUF weights as macOS-only MLX models.
15669.suggested_approach: Investigate model manifest publishing pipelines and registry validation rules. Ensure non-MLX GGUF models are not tagged with darwin-exclusive platform requirements, and verify Ollama client/server platform header reporting when requesting manifests.
likely_areas: registry/manifest publishing pipelines or backend model catalog metadata
cmd/cmd.go (pull request headers and platform attributes)
prerequisites: Access to model registry metadata or manifest publishing tooling
Environment with Linux and macOS to test manifest pull requests across platforms
implementation_steps: Inspect the manifest payloads returned by the registry for the reported tags (e.g., `qwen3.6:35b-a3b-coding-bf16`, `qwen3.6:27b-coding-nvfp4`) to check the `os` and `architecture` fields and layer annotations.
Verify whether the 412 response is generated server-side by the registry due to manifest OS restrictions or client-side platform validation.
If caused by model registry / catalog ingestion: update the publishing script/pipeline that converts and tags GGUF models so that non-MLX models omit the `os: darwin` restriction.

If caused by Ollama client/server compatibility checks or platform headers: update the pull logic in `server/manifest.go` or `server/download.go` to ensure platform restrictions are only enforced when models genuinely depend on macOS-exclusive frameworks (like MLX).
Re-tag/re-publish the affected model manifests without the restrictive macOS precondition.
Add regression tests verifying that GGUF quantization formats (nvfp4, mxfp8, bf16) can be queried and pulled on Linux and Windows platforms.

2475.title: Request to add  leo-hessianai to ollama
2475.feasibility_reason: Adding support for a new model family in Ollama typically involves defining the correct chat template, stop tokens, and model architecture mappings in the codebase or providing an officially supported Modelfile configuration.
2475.problem_summary: Users are requesting support and correct Modelfile configurations for LeoLM's leo-hessianai models (7B, 13B, 70B), as running them currently results in severe hallucination and incoherent outputs.
2475.root_cause_hypothesis: The hallucination issues stem from using base completion models instead of instruction/chat-tuned checkpoints (e.g., leo-hessianai-7b-chat), missing or malformed ChatML prompt templates (newline placement and system prompt defaults), and missing stop token definitions.
2475.suggested_approach: Provide canonical Modelfile templates configured for LeoLM's chat/bilingual variants using proper ChatML prompt formatting and stop tokens, or ingest the official leo-hessianai model weights and metadata into Ollama's official model library.
prerequisites: Access to Hugging Face repository LeoLM/leo-hessianai-*-chat or corresponding GGUF files from TheBloke/LeoLM
Local Ollama instance to test Modelfile generation, prompt formatting, and output quality
implementation_steps: Verify the model architecture and chat template specifications in `tokenizer_config.json` for `LeoLM/leo-hessianai-7b-chat` and `LeoLM/leo-hessianai-13b-chat-bilingual`.

Draft the standard ChatML Modelfile specifying the correct chat/bilingual GGUF source, correct ChatML template syntax (`<|im_start|>system
{{ .System }}<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>user
{{ .Prompt }}<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
`), and appropriate stop tokens (`<|im_end|>`, `<|im_start|>`).
Set default system instructions and sampling parameters (e.g. temperature, top_p) tailored to German/bilingual instruction following.
Build the model using `ollama create leo-hessianai -f Modelfile` and run test queries in German and English to ensure coherent generation without hallucination or infinite loops.
Document the recommended Modelfile configuration in community documentation or prepare the model definition for the Ollama library.

1036.title: `unexpected EOF` when running `ollama pull`
1036.feasibility_reason: The issue describes a well-defined download retry or resumption bug where an unexpected EOF can cause a download to get stuck, but a clear workaround exists and the error logs pinpoint the exact file and line (download.go:160).
1036.problem_summary: During 'ollama pull' or 'ollama run', model layer chunk downloads fail with 'unexpected EOF', leading to stalled downloads or 'max retries exceeded' errors.
1036.root_cause_hypothesis: The chunked/multipart blob downloader encounters truncated HTTP responses or closed connections mid-transfer, producing io.ErrUnexpectedEOF. Either the retry mechanism does not properly reset or resume from the byte offset for the affected part, reuses broken HTTP connections, or lacks adequate backoff and error recovery when network hiccups occur.
1036.suggested_approach: Inspect and harden the multipart download logic in `server/download.go`. Ensure each part download resets file offsets or reads cleanly on retry, uses exponential backoff, verifies that the HTTP transport does not keep alive stale connections after an unexpected EOF, and correctly propagates chunk completion or failure states so worker pools do not stall indefinitely.
prerequisites: Go development environment matching the repository version
Understanding of Go's net/http client, io.Reader/io.Copy, and Ollama's chunked download implementation
implementation_steps: Locate the chunk/part download routine in `server/download.go` around log statement `part %d attempt %d failed: %v, retrying`.
Examine the retry logic for parts: verify that the destination file write pointer/offset and read stream are properly reset to the part's initial range offset before retrying.

Ensure transient network errors like `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF`, `io.EOF`, and TLS connection resets trigger appropriate exponential backoff and request retries rather than immediately burning through attempt counts or hanging.
Verify the HTTP client configuration: ensure response bodies are properly closed and discarded on error so idle connections in the transport connection pool are invalidated if corrupted.
Check worker pool synchronization (e.g., errgroup, channels, or sync.WaitGroup) to ensure a failed or retried part does not deadlock remaining chunk workers.
Add or update unit and integration tests simulating interrupted HTTP streams (partial chunk transfer followed by EOF) to verify resilient resumption and completion.
